slides.text: This is the actual Glance Pay product demo, running in mock mode. On the left is the G two lens view: three short lines of text, because the glasses have no camera and no speaker. On the right is the paired phone control and debug screen.
The user makes an explicit start gesture. There is no always-on wake word. The phone screen shows the live state machine, now listening, and the lens invites the user to say, pay twelve fifty.

The phrase pay twelve fifty is parsed into twelve rupees and fifty paise. Two seeded merchants are about fifteen metres apart, so the app does not guess. It shows a pick list; the cursor moves with the ring and a tap selects.

After picking Cafe X, the confirm screen shows the amount in rupees and USDC, the merchant and a live countdown. A fresh quote is created at this moment. If it expires, the app re-quotes and asks for confirmation again rather than signing stale data.

One tap signs the intent and submits the payment. The lens says paying, while the phone audit log records each state with a timestamp and transaction hash. A second tap is ignored: confirmation is single-use.
The mock payout settles and the lens reads, paid twelve rupees fifty to Cafe X. This is a simulated testnet flow: no real wallet, no real UPI transfer and no funds moved.
Safety path. A wrong merchant hint produces a candidate list. The user makes a distinct cancel gesture, and the lens confirms that nothing was charged. The app never auto-pays.
Failure path. When the payout rail fails, the mock refunds the amount and the lens says, failed, refunded. The user is never left unsure whether money moved.
If the phone is far from any seeded merchant, the app says, no merchant nearby, and exits. It does not invent a merchant to keep the flow going.
Finally, a spoken amount above the five hundred rupee demo cap is refused at parse time, with a clear message on the lens. Glance Pay: hands-free payments, with safety built into every state.
